entry.title: ITEM_20170516001
entry.itemBody: The behavioral bias in which investors tend to avoid realizing losses but rather seek to realize gains is best described as:

answerFeedback.213e5651-5bd4-4a04-82a8-8803c4f29a2c: Correct. Behavioral biases in which investors tend to avoid realizing losses but rather seek to realize gains is the disposition effect.
answerFeedback.d9813fd6-44e2-4a6b-b87a-25dc738954fd: Incorrect. The disposition effect is a behavioral bias in which investors tend to avoid realizing losses but rather seek to realize gains.
answerFeedback.e7c7a77a-a282-4f6f-a0ec-cd8696fa9b2c: Incorrect. The gambler’s fallacy is a behavioral bias in which recent outcomes affect investors’ estimates of future probabilities.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516105
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about the forms of market efficiency is least accurate? If the form of market efficiency is:

answerFeedback.15d9adc8-da92-4d9e-8519-694983dfbe15: Incorrect. This statement is correct because the semi-strong-form of market efficiency also encompasses the weak-form; therefore, security prices reflect not only publicly known and available information but also all past market data.
answerFeedback.252a43f1-e5aa-4a86-8be9-4da4d0738345: Correct. If markets are strong-form efficient, prices reflect not only private information but also past market data and public information. If markets are weak-form efficient, investment strategies based on fundamental analysis of public information and past market data could achieve abnormal returns. The semi-strong-form of market efficiency also encompasses the weak form. Therefore, security prices reflect not only publicly known and available information but also all past market data.
answerFeedback.7e110003-d081-4765-bc2a-991eeb5a4364: Incorrect. This statement is correct because if markets are weak-form efficient only, investment strategies based on fundamental analysis could achieve abnormal returns.

choices.itemBody: A. strong, then prices reflect only private information.
B. semi-strong, then security prices fully reflect all past market data.
C. weak, then investment strategies based on fundamental analysis could achieve abnormal returns.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516107
entry.itemBody: A trader is able to obtain persistent abnormal returns by adopting an investment strategy that purchases stocks that have recently experienced high returns. This strategy exploits a market-pricing anomaly best described as:

answerFeedback.875e153c-8478-441c-b086-6c28658f6b57: Correct. A momentum anomaly occurs when securities that have experienced high short-term returns continue to generate higher returns in subsequent periods. Therefore, if a trader can obtain persistent abnormal returns by adopting an investment strategy that purchases stocks that have recently experienced high returns, then he or she is exploiting a momentum anomaly.
answerFeedback.c8db6465-41f4-493d-bb32-284c1c195890: Incorrect. The overreaction effect is a pricing anomaly that occurs when investors overreact to the release of unexpected public information, inflating (depressing) stock prices of companies releasing good (bad) information.
answerFeedback.e417e839-4b25-4137-bbb6-9988feb25b48: Incorrect. Data mining is not a market anomaly but a type of process that could be used to discover statistically significant price patterns.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516118
entry.itemBody: The weak-form market efficiency most accurately assumes that current security prices:

answerFeedback.bcfe703c-0292-4e19-9511-7b42bab3bd3d: Incorrect. It is the assumption of the semi-strong-form efficient market that security prices reflect all publicly known and available information.
answerFeedback.e646fe89-63ea-4645-bc4a-791a34e48ed5: Incorrect. It is the assumption of the strong-form efficient market that security prices fully reflect both public and private information.
answerFeedback.f418c968-d3d9-464f-a2d7-4529f4f3218f: Correct. In the weak-form efficient market hypothesis, security prices fully reflect all past market data including transactions by exchange specialists.

choices.itemBody: A. adjust rapidly to the release of all public information.
B. fully reflect all information from public and private sources.
C. fully reflect all past market information, including transactions by exchange specialists.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516161
entry.itemBody: In a highly efficient market, unexpected positive news on a stock is announced to the public. After this announcement, the difference between the market value and the intrinsic value of the stock will most likely:

answerFeedback.47ff3619-deca-460e-8e5f-89f507b4c70c: Incorrect. In a highly efficient market, (1) market value reflects new information quickly and rationally, and (2) an asset’s market value equals its intrinsic value. In an inefficient market, (1) the market value of a stock adjusts slowly to an unexpected news, and (2) there are probably discrepancies between market value and intrinsic value. Therefore, only in an inefficient market could the difference between market and intrinsic values increase after the announcement of an unexpected positive news.
answerFeedback.50838b23-78de-416d-be0a-a62c8afaa7be: Incorrect. In a highly efficient market, (1) market value reflects new information quickly and rationally, and (2) an asset’s market value equals its intrinsic value. In an inefficient market, (1) the market value of a stock adjusts slowly to an unexpected news, and (2) there are probably discrepancies between market value and intrinsic value. Therefore, only in an inefficient market could the difference between market and intrinsic values decrease after the announcement of an unexpected positive news.
answerFeedback.c3fd9a87-fcb3-4795-872e-820f5f6ae85c: Correct. In a highly efficient market, (1) market value reflects new information quickly and rationally, and (2) an asset’s market value equals its intrinsic value. Therefore, after the announcement, the difference between a stock’s market value and its intrinsic value will remain equal to zero because both market and intrinsic values adjust to reflect the unexpected news by the same amount and at the same time.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516163
entry.itemBody: If markets are only weak-form efficient, which of the following investment approaches is least likely to consistently earn abnormal profits?

answerFeedback.5ddf74d5-e857-44c5-a36a-b47d5b1c4eb4: Correct. In the weak-form efficient market hypothesis, security prices fully reflect all past market data, which refers to all historical price and trading volume information. Consequently, trading by looking at patterns of prices and volume from the past cannot consistently earn abnormal profits.
answerFeedback.d0e28750-3c46-458a-bfa2-0cf700471967: Incorrect. If markets are weak-form efficient, only past market data, but not private (nonpublic) information, are reflected in current prices. Consequently, exploiting nonpublic information can consistently earn abnormal profits. In most countries, such activity is prohibited.
answerFeedback.f32c9d20-0463-466f-a54a-257709c2b540: Incorrect. Fundamental analysis is the examination of publicly available information and the formulation of forecasts to estimate the intrinsic value of assets. If markets are weak-form efficient, only past market data, but not all publicly available information, are reflected in current prices. Consequently, buying and selling based on fundamental analysis can consistently earn abnormal profits.

choices.itemBody: B. Trading based on patterns of prices and volume
C. Buying and selling based on fundamental analysis

entry.title: ITEM_20170516013
entry.itemBody: An observation that stocks with above average price-to-earnings ratios have consistently underperformed those with below average price-to-earnings ratios least likely contradicts which form of market efficiency?

answerFeedback.24241baf-281e-4afd-99cd-feca9c29dfa0: Incorrect. The data on price-to-earnings ratios are publicly available, and the related anomaly therefore is a contradiction to the semi-strong and strong forms of market efficiency.
answerFeedback.8c154058-2863-4070-a800-bc139cfb0c58: Correct. The observation that stocks with high above average price-to-earnings ratios have consistently underperformed those with below average price-to-earnings ratios is a cross-sectional anomaly. It is a contradiction to the semi-strong form of market efficiency and strong form market efficiency because all the information used to categorize stocks by their price-to-earnings ratios is publicly available. It is not a contradiction to weak form market efficiency.
answerFeedback.93976d24-1e72-4381-941b-6f187d503cfd: Incorrect. The data on price-to-earnings ratios are publicly available, and the related anomaly therefore is a contradiction to the semi-strong form of market efficiency.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516052
entry.itemBody: Which of the following situations will most likely promote an increase in market efficiency?

answerFeedback.0ebfcff7-4dc9-406a-af0c-4ba2b18928f5: Correct. Information availability (e.g., active financial news media or information regarding trading activity and traded companies) and financial disclosure should promote or increase market efficiency.
answerFeedback.14080b37-f704-42a1-b3ff-e418fc699c22: Incorrect. Arbitrage is a set of transactions that produces riskless profits. Arbitrageurs are traders who engage in such trades to benefit from pricing discrepancies (inefficiencies) in markets. Such trading activity contributes to market efficiency. If arbitrage opportunities increase, it means that there are either more pricing discrepancies or fewer arbitrageurs (or both), and this situation will lead to a reduction in market efficiency.
answerFeedback.6766b729-bd6f-42c8-a252-3f7fa0457530: Incorrect. A decrease in trading activity can cause or accentuate other market imperfections that impede market efficiency.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516073
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements is most accurate in an efficient market?

answerFeedback.b7ee6757-7098-4eca-9ed0-6471059d48b5: Incorrect. In an efficient market, securities market prices reflect their fundamental values, so opportunities for active strategies to achieve excess risk adjusted returns may not exist.
answerFeedback.c7c8a8e7-561a-4768-b716-d4888827e929: Incorrect. An efficient market is a market in which asset prices reflect information quickly, not over time.
answerFeedback.ea57053f-1643-4a29-b91e-78800b4ebe31: Correct. In an efficient market, market participants will process available information, and those with opposite views will trade among each other until securities market prices fully reflect their fundamental values. An efficient market is thus a market in which asset prices reflect all past and present information.

choices.itemBody: A. Securities market prices fully reflect their fundamental values.
B. Active strategies will lead to excess risk-adjusted portfolio returns.
C. Securities market prices respond over time to changes in economic information.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516078
entry.itemBody:
An internal evaluation of the trading behavior of three fund managers of a mutual fund company during the past year has revealed the following:

• Manager X:

Was slower than peers when reacting to changes in information

• Manager Y: 

Rarely realized investment losses but realized most of the investment gains

• Manager Z: 

 Tended to overreact by disliking losses more than liking comparable gains

Which of the three managers most likely displayed the disposition effect bias?

answerFeedback.4dd25c33-a877-436b-810c-650b6b59d77e: Correct. The disposition effect relates to the behavioral bias in which investors tend to avoid realizing losses but, rather, seek to realize gains. Manager Y has displayed this bias.
answerFeedback.702323a3-1ba5-46a0-b51f-cc7a782496d8: Incorrect. Manager X’s behavior of reacting slow to changes is consistent with conservatism.
answerFeedback.b3bd6317-823f-45d9-a1c9-93ddb58e0ea9: Incorrect. Over-reacting, including a dislike for losses more than liking comparable gains, displayed by Manager Z is reflective of a behavioral bias called loss aversion.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516079
entry.itemBody: Arbitrage activity will most likely be higher in securities markets:

answerFeedback.11f53fe1-d2f3-40b2-a23f-f6c0719e49c5: Incorrect. High trading costs (transaction costs and information-acquisition costs) would negatively impact the potential profits thereby impeding the arbitrage activity.
answerFeedback.229dd215-cfef-473b-b6b0-25cc43b0234a: Incorrect. In an efficient market security prices tend to be closely aligned with the intrinsic values. Thus, arbitrage activity will be less in markets that are efficient.
answerFeedback.e6b7ae9d-718b-45d0-b243-c366976c1e04: Correct. Short selling helps in price discovery. Arbitrageurs benefit from pricing discrepancies (inefficiencies); therefore, arbitrage activity will be higher in markets with no restrictions on short selling.

choices.itemBody: B. with no restrictions on short selling.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516080
entry.itemBody: If securities markets are semi-strong-form efficient, the most appropriate role of a portfolio manager is to:

answerFeedback.7a6e66a8-6ad9-4c95-bc1d-754ac758a14e: Incorrect. The semi-strong-form efficiency assumes that prices reflect all publicly known and available information, and therefore efforts to analyze publicly available information is futile.
answerFeedback.9d184d42-50b6-4422-83d1-890a14fc72d3: Incorrect. Exploiting trading rules and serial correlations would not be feasible if markets are weak-form efficient, leave alone semi-strong-form efficiency.
answerFeedback.caffa6f8-d8c2-4152-becd-cb430e07fa3e: Correct. If markets are semi-strong-form efficient (which also encompasses weak-form efficiency), the role of a portfolio manager is not necessarily to beat the market, but rather to establish and manage a portfolio consistent with the portfolio’s objectives, with appropriate diversification and asset allocation, while taking into consideration the risk preferences and tax situation of the investor.

choices.itemBody: A. invest by analyzing publicly available information to consistently generate abnormal returns.
B. manage portfolios with appropriate diversification and asset allocation, taking into consideration investor preferences.
C. exploit appropriate trading rules and serial correlations for achieving excess returns.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516082
entry.itemBody: After the public announcement of the merger of two firms, an investor makes abnormal returns by going long on the target firm and short on the acquiring firm. This most likely violates which form of market efficiency?

answerFeedback.57a0168f-f53a-42ca-82ee-8d89250c00ce: Incorrect. A market that is not semi-strong-form efficient is also not strong-form efficient. Thus, violating the semi-strong-form efficiency also implies violating the strong-form efficiency.
answerFeedback.9a364cce-121e-42ad-b4b5-760ca61dddab: Incorrect. The market could still be weak-form efficient, as past prices are not being used to make abnormal profits. Thus, we cannot say that the weak-form market efficiency has been violated.
answerFeedback.9c9273e1-0470-415a-a227-ccf5512a61df: Correct. In a semi-strong-form efficient market, prices adjust quickly and accurately to new information. In this case, prices would quickly adjust to the merger announcement, and if the market is a semi-strong-form efficient market, investors acting after the merger announcement would not be able to earn abnormal returns. Therefore, the market is not semi-strong-form efficient. A market that is not semi-strong-form efficient is also not strong-form efficient. Thus, violating the semi-strong-form efficiency also implies violating the strong-form efficiency. However, the market could still be weak-form efficient because past prices are not being used to make abnormal profits. Thus, we cannot say that the weak-form market efficiency has been violated.

entry.title: ITEM_20170516166
entry.itemBody: The value effect market-pricing anomaly most likely occurs when stocks that have below-average price-to-earnings and market-to-book ratios, as well as above-average dividend yields, consistently outperform:

answerFeedback.1d4dbcf7-5e28-4524-976f-3cd3f77b33df: Correct. The value effect occurs when value stocks, which are generally referred to as stocks that have below-average price-to-earnings and market-to-book ratios, as well as above-average dividend yields, outperform growth stocks consistently and for long periods.
answerFeedback.7431315c-495b-4007-a472-f4594465254f: Incorrect. It is the size effect, not the value effect, that compares returns with respect to large-cap stocks.
answerFeedback.e02cedff-cd75-4eaa-bb1a-6c11500be60d: Incorrect. Value effect does not compare stocks on the basis of earnings surprises. It is the “earnings surprise” anomaly that compares companies on the basis of the unexpected part of the earnings announcement.

choices.itemBody: C. stocks that have had negative earnings surprises.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2021.07-Equity-Young-02
entry.itemBody: If a security’s intrinsic value is $55 per share and is currently selling for $50 per share, the security is:

answerFeedback.9afb580b-74a8-4f58-899a-af0e86f12120: Incorrect because the security’s market price is less than its intrinsic value, indicating that it is undervalued. The dividend discount model can be used to estimate an asset’s intrinsic value.
answerFeedback.e932e380-75a1-4b2f-aaae-f0851930f919: Correct because the security’s market price is less than its intrinsic value, indicating that it is undervalued. The dividend discount model can be used to estimate an asset’s intrinsic value.
answerFeedback.ebfd383d-3559-4e74-a106-fe658ee922fd: Incorrect because the security’s market price is less than its intrinsic value, indicating that it is undervalued. The dividend discount model can be used to estimate an asset’s intrinsic value.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-07998
entry.itemBody: Which of the following factors would most likely increase market efficiency? Limits on:

answerFeedback.07d26df7-3aa7-41b5-965b-9898513170a2: Incorrect because restrictions on short selling limit arbitrage trading, which impedes market efficiency.
answerFeedback.e33d1384-c156-438a-a326-5094f9f0a777: Correct because transaction costs are incurred in trading to exploit any perceived market inefficiency. If there are limits on transaction costs, more investors would be encouraged to trade. This brings about increased number of market participants which in turn contributes to market efficiency. One of the most critical factors contributing to the degree of efficiency in a market is the number of market participants.
answerFeedback.ee258626-9d36-44c4-8909-d9c64d99df17: Incorrect because a lack of trading activity can cause or accentuate other market imperfections that impede market efficiency. In fact, in many of these markets, such as China, trading in many of the listed stocks is restricted for foreigners. By nature, this limitation reduces the number of market participants, restricts the potential for trading activity, and hence reduces market efficiency.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-05953
entry.itemBody: If investors can successfully predict future asset prices based on past prices, markets are most likely:

answerFeedback.080b0116-0808-44e9-93af-afa1c55e3351: Correct because under all forms of market efficiency past trading data are already reflected in current prices and investors cannot predict future price changes by extrapolating prices or patterns of prices from the past. Therefore, if investors can predict future asset prices based on past prices, markets are inefficient.
answerFeedback.386043ba-d06e-4d6d-b271-f83e4dd540bc: Incorrect because in the weak-form efficient market hypothesis, security prices fully reflect all past market data, which refers to all historical prices and trading volume information. If markets are weak-form efficient, past trading data are already reflected in current prices and investors cannot predict future price changes by extrapolating prices or patterns of prices from the past.
answerFeedback.43de9233-725d-4900-9476-8d5e487c08d9: Incorrect because under all forms of market efficiency past trading data are already reflected in current prices and investors cannot predict future price changes by extrapolating prices or patterns of prices from the past.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q1
entry.itemBody: The short-term shutdown point of production for a firm operating under perfect competition will most likely occur when:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The firm should shut down production when marginal revenue is less than or equal to average variable cost.

choices.itemBody: A. price is equal to average total cost.
B. marginal revenue is equal to marginal cost.
C. marginal revenue is equal to average variable costs.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q2
entry.itemBody: Under conditions of perfect competition, a company will break even when market price is equal to the minimum point of the:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. A company is said to break even if its total revenue is equal to its total cost. Under conditions of perfect competition, a company will break even when market price is equal to the minimum point of the average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q3
entry.itemBody: A company will shut down production in the short run if total revenue is less than total:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A company will shut down production in the short run when total revenue is below total variable costs.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q4
entry.itemBody: A company has total variable costs of $4 million and fixed costs of $3 million. Based on this information, the company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue is at least:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. A company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue is equal to or greater than total cost. Because total costs are $7 million ($4 million variable costs and $3 million fixed costs), the company will stay in the market in the long term if total revenue equals at least $7 million.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q5
entry.itemBody: When total revenue is greater than total variable costs but less than total costs, in the short term, a firm will most likely:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. When total revenue is enough to cover variable costs but not total fixed costs in full, the firm can survive in the short run but would not be able to maintain financial solvency in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q6
entry.itemBody: Under conditions of perfect competition, in the long run, firms will most likely earn:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Competition should drive prices down to long-run marginal cost, resulting in only normal profits being earned.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q7
entry.itemBody: A firm that increases its quantity produced without any change in per-unit cost is experiencing:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Output increases in the same proportion as input increases occur at constant returns to scale.

choices.itemBody: C. constant returns to scale. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 2 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q8
entry.itemBody: A company is experiencing economies of scale when:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Economies of scale occur if, as the firm increases output, cost per unit of production falls. Graphically, this definition translates into an LRAC with a negative slope.

choices.itemBody: A. cost per unit increases as output increases.
B. it is operating at a point on the LRAC curve at which the slope is negative.
C. it is operating beyond the minimum point on the long-run average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q9
entry.itemBody: Diseconomies of scale most likely result from:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. As the firm increases output, diseconomies of scale and higher average total costs can result when business functions and product lines overlap or are duplicated.

choices.itemBody: B. overlap of business functions and product lines.
C. discounted prices on resources when buying in larger quantities.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q10
entry.itemBody: A firm is operating beyond minimum efficient scale in a perfectly competitive industry. To maintain long-term viability, the most likely course of action for the firm is to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The firm operating at greater than long-run efficient scale is subject to diseconomies of scale. It should plan to decrease its level of production.

choices.itemBody: A. operate at the current level of production.
B. increase its level of production to gain economies of scale.
C. decrease its level of production to the minimum point on the long-run average total cost curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q11
entry.itemBody: Companies most likely have a well-defined supply function when the market structure is:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A company in a perfectly competitive market must accept whatever price the market dictates. The marginal cost schedule of a company in a perfectly competitive market determines its supply function.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q12
entry.itemBody: Aquarius, Inc. is the dominant company and the price leader in its market. One of the other companies in the market attempts to gain market share by undercutting the price set by Aquarius. The market share of Aquarius will most likely:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. As prices decrease, smaller companies will leave the market rather than sell below cost. The market share of Aquarius, the price leader, will increase. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 11 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q13
entry.itemBody: Over time, the market share of the dominant company in an oligopolistic market will most likely:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The dominant company’s market share tends to decrease as profits attract entry by other companies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q14
entry.itemBody: Successful advertising and product differentiation are most likely to have a positive impact on the economic profits of a producer under:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Advertising and product differentiation are most likely to have a positive impact on the economic profits of producers under monopolistic competition. The monopoly aspect of this structure arises from the ability to differentiate its product.

choices.itemBody: C. monopoly. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 3 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q15
entry.itemBody: The two dominant supermarket chains in the area are attempting to increase their market share by moving to 24-hour service instead of closing at 9 p.m. every night. The strategic outcomes and payoff matrix that arise from their actions are depicted in the diagram (with the shaded sections representing payoffs for Chain 2). The most likely Nash equilibrium strategy for the two chains is for:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Each company will consider the other’s reaction in selecting its strategy. Using the following summary, it is best for both chains to provide 24-hour service. Chain Consideration Best Decision If it opens for 24 hours, it will see a higher payoff regardless of what Chain 2 does. Chain 2 Chain 2 1 Closes at 9 p.m. Opens for 24 hours Open for 24 hours Chain 1 earns 540 instead of 180 Chain 1 earns 108 instead of 55 If it opens for 24 hours, it will see a higher payoff regardless of what Chain 1 does. Chain 1 Chain 1 2 Chain 1 Closes at 9 p.m. Chain 1 Opens for 24 hours Open for 24 hours Chain 2 earns 592 instead of 290 Chain 2 earns 140 instead of 75

choices.itemBody: A. both chains to open for 24 hours.
B. only Chain 2 to open for 24 hours.
C. both chains to close at 9 p.m.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q16
entry.itemBody: Six companies in an industry have the following market shares: Company A B C D E F Market Share (%) 30 25 16 12 10 7 If Companies D and F merge into a new Company, G, the industry’s three -company concentration ratio would be closest to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The concentration ratio for the top three companies would be 74%: A (30%) + B (25%) + G (12% + 7%).

choices.itemBody: C. 74%. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 4 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q17
entry.itemBody: Assume that two firms in a duopoly enter into a collusive agreement in an attempt to form a cartel and restrict output, raise prices, and increase profits. According to the Nash equilibrium, a low price is most likely charged by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The market outcomes for two firms in a duopoly is shown in the diagram. The lower left hand quadrant is the Nash solution when there is no collusion. However, with collusion, if ArcCo shares at least enough of its profit in the bottom right quadrant to provide BatCo more than it would receive in the lower left, it will be the optimal solution for the pair: the maximum joint profits will arise where both firms charge high prices for the product. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 12 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q18
entry.itemBody: Which characteristic is a firm least likely to exhibit if it faces a downward sloping demand curve for its product(s), many competitors, and zero economic profits in the long run?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The characteristics of monopolistic competition include a large number of competitors, low pricing power, and the production of differentiated products (through advertising and other non -price strategies), but these still result in some pricing power. The ease of entry results in zero economic profits in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q19
entry.itemBody: With its existing production facilities, a monopolist firm can produce up to 100 units. It faces the following demand and cost schedules: Output (Units) Price ($/Unit) Total Costs ($) 0 3,000 600 20 2,800 10,600 40 2,600 32,600 60 2,400 66,600 80 2,200 112,600 100 2,000 170,600 The optimal output level for this producer (in units) is closest to:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The optimal output level is 60 units because that level produces the highest profit: Output (Units) Price ($/Unit) Total Revenue ($) Total Costs ($) Profit ($) 20 2,800 56,000 10,600 45,400 40 2,600 1,04,000 32,600 71,400 60 2,400 1,44,000 66,600 77,400 80 2,200 1,76,000 1,12,600 63,400 100 2,000 2,00,000 1,70,600 29,400

choices.itemBody: C. 20. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 5 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q20
entry.itemBody: Three firms operate under perfect competition, producing 900 units of the same product but using different production technologies. Each company’s cost structure is indicated in the table: Company X Y Z Total Variable Costs $2,700 $3,600 $4,500 Total Fixed Costs 2,700 1,800 900 Total Costs $5,400 $5,400 $5,400 Which of the following statements is most accurate? If the unit selling price is:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Revenue–Cost Relationship Short-Run Decision Long-Term Decision TR ≥ TC Stay in market Stay in market TR > TVC but TR < TFC + TVC Stay in market Exit market TR < TVC Shut down production Exit market TR = Total Revenue; TC = Total Costs; TVC = Total Variable Costs; TFC = Total Fixed Costs Hence, if the selling price is $3.00, total revenue for all firms will be $3.00/unit × 900 units = $2,700. Only Firm X’s variable costs are covered and it should continue operating, while Firms Y and Z should immediately shut down production.

choices.itemBody: A. $6.00, all firms should exit the market in the long run.
B. $4.50, all firms should continue to operate in the short run, but exit the market in the long run if these conditions are expected to persist.
C. $3.00, Firm X should continue to operate in the short run, but Firms Y and Z should shut down production.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q21
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about a downward -sloping long -run average cost (LRAC) curve is most accurate? A downward -sloping LRAC curve is representative of a firm experiencing:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. When the LRAC curve is downward sloping, it means the firm is producing units at lower average costs per unit as production levels rise. This situation represents economies of scale in production.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q22
entry.itemBody: Firms operating under a monopolistic competition market structure most likely:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because under monopolistic competition, the products offered by each seller are close substitutes for the products offered by other firms, and each firm tries to make its product look different.

choices.itemBody: B. benefit from high barriers to entry.
C. sell products that are close substitutes for those offered by other firms.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q23
entry.itemBody: A market structure characterized by homogeneous/standardized product differentiation is best described as:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Perfect competition and oligopoly are characterized by homogeneous/standardized product differentiation. Market Structure Degree of Product Differentiation Perfect competition Homogeneous/standardized Monopolistic competition Differentiated Oligopoly Homogeneous/standardized Monopoly Unique product Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 13 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q24
entry.itemBody: In a perfectly competitive market, a firm's breakeven point is the minimum point of the:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because economists refer to the minimum AVC point as the shutdown point and the minimum ATC point as the breakeven point.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q25
entry.itemBody: In the long run, a monopolistically competitive firm: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 6 of 16

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because in the hybrid market of monopolistic competition, zero economic profit in long-run equilibrium resembles perfect competition. However, the long -run level of output, Q1, is less than Q2, which corresponds to the minimum average cost of production an d would be the long -run level of output in a perfectly competitive market.

choices.itemBody: B. faces a perfectly elastic demand curve.
C. produces at a higher level of average cost than the minimum average cost.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q26
entry.itemBody: In an oligopoly market, which of the following best describes the situation when firms have no incentive to deviate from their current pricing strategy based on the anticipated choices of competitors?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the Nash equilibrium is present when two or more participants in a non - cooperative game have no incentive to deviate from their respective equilibrium strategies after they have considered and anticipated their opponent’s rational choices or strategies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q27
entry.itemBody: In which of the following market structures does marginal revenue equal price?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because only in perfect competition does the marginal revenue equal price. In the remaining structures, price generally exceeds marginal revenue because a firm can sell more units only by reducing the per unit price.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q28
entry.itemBody: The perfectly competitive firm's supply curve is its long-run:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the long-run marginal cost schedule is the perfectly competitive firm's supply curve.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q29
entry.itemBody: To calculate the Herfindahl–Hirschman index:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because to avoid the known issues with concentration ratios, economists O.C. Herfindahl and A.O. Hirschman suggested an index where the market shares of the top N companies are first squared and then added.

choices.itemBody: A. add the market shares of the largest firms.
B. add the market shares of the largest firms and then square the sum.
C. square the market shares of the largest firms and then add the results.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q30
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information about three markets: Number of Sellers Non-Price Competition Market 1 Many None Market 2 Few Strong Market 3 Many Strong Which market is most likely an oligopoly?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in an oligopoly market there are a small number of potential sellers and products are often highly differentiated through marketing, features, and other non-price strategies.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q31
entry.itemBody: Monopolistic competition is best characterized by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because for a monopolistically competitive firm: suppliers differentiate their products through advertising and other non-price strategies.

choices.itemBody: A. high barriers to entry and exit.
B. a small number of buyers and sellers.
C. product differentiation through non-price strategies. Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 7 of 16

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q32
entry.itemBody: If a perfectly competitive industry becomes monopolistically competitive, each firm's long-run average total cost per unit sold will most likely:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because unlike long-run equilibrium in perfect competition, in the market of monopolistic competition, the equilibrium position is at a higher level of average cost than the level of output that minimizes average cost. Average cost does not reach its minim um until output level Q2 is achieved. Under perfect competition a product is produced at the efficient quantity (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) and average total cost is minimized. The demand faced by each firm is perfectly elastic (ho rizontal demand curve). However, under monopolistic competition the demand curve is downward sloping and the quantity produced (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) is not where average total cost is minimized. Thus, average total cost is lower under perfect competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q33
entry.itemBody: If a monopolistically competitive industry becomes perfectly competitive, each firm's long-run average total cost per unit sold will most likely:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because under perfect competition a product is produced at the efficient quantity (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) and the average total cost is Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 14 of 16 minimized. The demand curve faced by each firm is perfectly elastic (horizontal demand curve). However, under monopolistic competition the demand curve is downward sloping and the quantity produced (marginal revenue equals marginal cost) is not where average total cost is minimized. Thus, average total cost is lower under perfect competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q34
entry.itemBody: In the short run, the shutdown point of a company with a total variable cost of $3 million and a total fixed cost of $5 million is when total revenue declines to:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because as long as the firm’s revenues cover at least its variable cost, the firm is better off continuing to operate. If price is greater than average variable cost (AVC), the firm is covering not only all of its variable cost but also a portion of fixed cost. Also, average revenue (AR) is revenue per unit.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q35
entry.itemBody: A firm in a market environment characterized by monopolistic competition is most likely to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. as the name implies, monopolistic competition is a hybrid market structure. The most distinctive factor in monopolistic competition is product differentiation. Although the market is made up of many firms that compose the product group, each producer attempt s to distinguish its product from that of the others, and product differentiation is accomplished in a variety of ways.

choices.itemBody: A. continue to experience economic profit in the long run.
B. have a well-defined supply function reflecting its marginal and average costs.
C. have many competitors each following its own product differentiation strategy.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q36
entry.itemBody: In long-run equilibrium, the perfectly competitive firm's supply curve is best represented by the firm's long-run:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the long-run marginal cost schedule is the perfectly competitive firm’s supply curve. The firm’s demand curve is dictated by the aggregate market’s equilibrium price. The basic rule of profit maximization is that MR = MC, as is the case in long-run equilibrium.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q37
entry.itemBody: Under monopolistic competition, a firm's supply curve is represented by:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because in perfect competition, the firm’s supply schedule is represented by the marginal cost schedule. In monopolistic competition, there is no well -defined supply function. The information used to determine the appropriate level of output is based on the intersection of MC and MR. However, the price that will be charged is based on the market demand schedule. The firm’s supply curve should measure the quantity the firm is willing to supply at various prices. That information is not represented by either marginal cost or average cost.

choices.itemBody: C. neither average cost nor marginal cost.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q38
entry.itemBody: Under which of the following market structures are pricing strategies most likely influenced by the expected reaction of other firms?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the oligopoly market structure is based on a relatively small number of firms supplying the market. The small number of firms in the market means that each firm must consider what retaliatory strategies the other firms will pursue when prices and production levels change. Consider the pricing behavior of commercial airline companies. Pricing strategies and route scheduling are based on the expected reaction of the other carriers in similar markets.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q39
entry.itemBody: Each oligopoly firm faces an individual demand curve under: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 8 of 16

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in an oligopoly market where collusion is present, the aggregate market demand curve is divided up by the individual production participants. Under non-colluding market conditions, each firm faces an individual demand curve.

choices.itemBody: C. both colluding and non-colluding market conditions.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q40
entry.itemBody: In theory, under which of the following market structures do firms have the least control over price?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because from the perspective of the owners of the firm, the most desirable market structure is that with the most control over price, because this control can lead to large profits. Monopoly and oligopoly markets offer the greatest Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 15 of 16 potential control over price; monopolistic competition offers less control. Firms operating under perfectly competitive market conditions have no control over price.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q41
entry.itemBody: According to the Cournot assumption, in an oligopoly market each firm determines its profit-maximizing production level by assuming that other firms will:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because in the Cournot assumption, each firm determines its profit - maximizing production level by assuming that the other firms' output will not change. This assumption simplifies pricing strategy because there is no need to guess what the other firm will do to retaliate.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q42
entry.itemBody: Which of the following indicators suggest(s) a monopoly market?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the concentration ratio is the sum of the market shares of the largest N firms. This number is always between zero (perfect competition) and 100 percent (monopoly).

choices.itemBody: B. A Herfindahl–Hirschman index of zero only
C. Both a concentration ratio of 100% and a Herfindahl–Hirschman index of zero

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q43
entry.itemBody: The Herfindahl–Hirschman index is calculated based on:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because in calculating the Herfindahl –Hirschman index the market shares of the top N companies are first squared and then added. If one firm controls the whole market (a monopoly), the Herfindahl –Hirschman index (HHI) equals 1. If there are M firms in the industry with equal market shares, then the HHI equals (1/M).

choices.itemBody: B. elasticity of demand in the market.
C. probability of new entry into the market.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q44
entry.itemBody: Which of the following market structures has high barriers to entry?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the characteristics of oligopoly markets include: entry into the market is difficult, with fairly high costs and significant barriers to competition.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q45
entry.itemBody: Under which of the following market structures is product differentiation most important?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because monopolistic competition is also highly competitive; however, it is considered a form of imperfect competition. The competitive characteristic is a notably large number of firms, while the monopoly aspect is the result of product differentiation. That is, if the seller can convince consumers that its product is uniquely different from other, similar products, then the seller can exercise some degree of pricing power over the market.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q46
entry.itemBody: An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about a firm operating in a perfectly competitive market: Total variable costs 700 Total fixed costs 400 If the firm's total revenue is $1,000 million, the firm should: Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 9 of 16

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because when TR total revenue is enough to cover TVC (total variable costs) but not all of TFC total fixed costs, the firm can continue to produce in the short run but will be unable to maintain financial solvency in the long run. TR is $1,000 which is greater than TVC of $700, but not enough to cover the firm's TFC of $400. Therefore, the firm will exit the market in the long run.

choices.itemBody: A. stay in the market in both the short run and long run.
B. stay in the market in the short run and exit the market in the long run.
C. shut down production in the short run and exit the market in the long run.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q47
entry.itemBody: A perfectly competitive market structure:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because profits under the conditions of perfect competition are driven to the required rate of return paid by the entrepreneur to borrow capital from investors (so-called normal profit or rental cost of capital).

choices.itemBody: B. causes all industries to ultimately fail due to lack of profits.
C. drives company profits to the investors' required rate of return.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q48
entry.itemBody: In the short run, a firm most likely shuts down production when:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because the firm must cover its variable cost to remain in business in the short run. If TR cannot cover TVC, the firm shuts down production to minimize loss. The loss would be equal to the amount of fixed cost.

choices.itemBody: B. sunk costs are greater than total revenue.
C. total revenue is less than total variable cost.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q49
entry.itemBody: A disadvantage of the concentration ratio is that it:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because a disadvantage of the concentration ratio is that it tends to be unaffected by mergers among the top market incumbents. For example, if the largest and second-largest incumbents merge, the pricing power of the combined entity is Firms and Market Structures Faculty: Page 16 of 16 likely to be larger than that of the two pre-existing companies. But the concentration ratio may not change much.

choices.itemBody: A. requires a large number of time-series observations.
B. is largely unaffected by mergers among the top market incumbents.
C. requires the specification of the explanatory variables used in regression analysis.

entry.title: 2027-Mod41-Q50
entry.itemBody: A manufacturing company expanded in a new region by setting up local assembly lines and hiring local staff. Two years later, the company's sale had grown as expected but operating margin had shrunk from 15 to 12 percent. The company:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the company is most likely suffering from diseconomies of scale. It is having to duplicate all costs in each location, and by targeting different demographics, it has added additional costs for inputs and marketing. Therefore, the company’s fixed costs have increased faster than output, and the economic result is diseconomies of scale.

choices.itemBody: A. has yet to reach its breakeven volume.
B. is suffering from diseconomies of scale.
